# hyperping_statuspage_sso_connection (Resource)

Manages an OpenID Connect SSO connection that visitors of private status pages sign in with (Auth0, Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak…). A status page uses it through `settings.authentication.sso_connection_uuid`.

Hyperping checks the issuer's discovery document and the client credentials before saving: a configuration the identity provider refuses fails at `apply` and creates nothing. Register `redirect_uri` as an allowed callback URL in the identity provider. A connection is billed like one created in the dashboard. SAML connections are set up in the dashboard; read them with the `hyperping_statuspage_sso_connection` data source.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# OpenID Connect connection for a private status page (Auth0 here; any
# OpenID Connect identity provider works: Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak…).
variable "auth0_client_id" {
  type = string
}

variable "auth0_client_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "hyperping_statuspage_sso_connection" "auth0" {
  name          = "Auth0"
  issuer        = "https://acme.eu.auth0.com/"
  client_id     = var.auth0_client_id
  client_secret = var.auth0_client_secret

  # Only accounts with these email domains can sign in (omit for any).
  allowed_domains = ["acme.com"]
}

# Visitors of this page sign in through Auth0.
resource "hyperping_statuspage" "internal" {
  name             = "Internal Status"
  hosted_subdomain = "acme-internal"

  settings = {
    name      = "Internal Status"
    languages = ["en"]

    authentication = {
      sso_connection_uuid = hyperping_statuspage_sso_connection.auth0.id
    }
  }
}

# Register this URL as an allowed callback URL of the Auth0 application.
output "auth0_callback_url" {
  value = hyperping_statuspage_sso_connection.auth0.redirect_uri
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `client_id` (String) Client ID of the application registered in the identity provider.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) Client secret of the application. Write-only on the API side: Hyperping never returns it, so a secret rotated outside Terraform is not detected. After `terraform import`, the next `apply` sends it once.
- `issuer` (String) Issuer URL of the identity provider: the address before `/.well-known/openid-configuration` (e.g. `https://acme.eu.auth0.com/`). A bare domain also works. Hyperping stores the issuer the identity provider publishes; the configuration keeps its own spelling as long as it names the same identity provider (trailing slash, `https://`, discovery path). After `terraform import` the issuer reads back as stored: write it that way, or the first `apply` makes an update that changes nothing on the Hyperping side.
- `name` (String) Name of the connection, shown in the dashboard.

### Optional

- `allowed_domains` (List of String) Email domains allowed to sign in (e.g. `["acme.com"]`). Empty = any account the identity provider signs in. When omitted, the domains set in the dashboard are kept.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Connection ID (`sso_…`). Set it as `settings.authentication.sso_connection_uuid` of a `hyperping_statuspage`.
- `redirect_uri` (String) Callback URL to register in the identity provider (`https://api.hyperping.io/v1/auth/sso/oidc/callback`, or `https://api.eu.hyperping.io/...` for EU accounts).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an OpenID Connect connection by its ID. The client secret is never
# returned by the API: keep it in the configuration, the next apply sends it once.
terraform import hyperping_statuspage_sso_connection.auth0 sso_abc123xyz
```
